test_title: PYST 6: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

​He said, "My brother is sleeping."

options.text: He said his brother is sleeping.
He said that his brother was sleeping.
He said that his brother had slept.
He said his brother has been sleeping.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "My brother is sleeping."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"is sleeping" becomes "was sleeping"**
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the **Present Continuous** tense in direct speech changes to **Past Continuous** in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun "My" becomes "his"**
 
 
• The first-person possessive adjective "My" changes to the third-person "his" to refer back to the speaker ("He").
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The quotation marks and comma are removed.
 
• The conjunction "that" is added to connect the reporting verb to the reported clause.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He said that his brother was sleeping.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He said his brother is sleeping." 

 
 
• Incorrect because the tense remained in the present continuous, failing to back-shift to the past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said that his brother had slept." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "had slept" is the **Past Perfect** tense, which would correspond to a past simple or present perfect in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said his brother has been sleeping." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "has been sleeping" is **Present Perfect Continuous**, which does not match the original continuous action.
